Analyze a cantilever beam using Euler–Bernoulli beam theory with small deflections and linear elastic behavior.
Use N–mm–MPa units.
The beam has length L = 1800 mm, fixed at x = 0 and free at x = L.
Material is structural steel with Young's modulus E = 200000 MPa.
The second moment of area is constant I = 1200000 mm^4.
A downward point load P = 2000 N is applied at the free end.
The bending moment varies linearly as M(x) = P(L − x), from zero at the free end to PL at the fixed end.
Use the standard Euler–Bernoulli cantilever solutions with no simplifications.
Compute the free-end slope as θ = P·L² / (2·E·I) = 2000·1800² / (2·200000·1200000) = 0.0135 rad ≈ 0.773°.
Compute the free-end deflection as δ = P·L³ / (3·E·I) = 2000·1800³ / (3·200000·1200000) = 16.2 mm downward.
Report the slope in radians and degrees, and the deflection in mm.
